senses.gloss: भद्र- + आसन भद्र- + आसन, n. 1. a throne. 2. a peculiar posture, in which abstract meditation is performed by a devotee.
भद्र-काली भद्र-काली, f. 1. a name of Durgā. 2. a fragrant grass, Cyperus.
भद्र- + कुम्भ भद्र- + कुम्भ, m. a golden jar filled with water from a holy place.
भाद्र- + पद भाद्र- + पद, 1. m. the month Bhādra. 2. f. दा, a name common to the twentysixth and twenty-seventh lunar asterisms.
भद्र- + पीठ भद्र- + पीठ, a throne, Vikr. 87, 13.
भदन्त भदन्त, m. A Bauddha mendicant.

भद्र भद् + र (cf. भन्द्),
 I. adj., f. रा.
 1. Excellent, best, Vikr. 27, 10; Pañc. 146, 17.
 2. Worthy, dear, Daśak. in Chr. 185, 11.
 3. Pious.
 4. Happy, Vikr. d. 163; propitious, Hit. 22, 5, M.M.
 5. Comparat. भद्रतर, Better, Hit. 80, 5.
 II. भद्र + म्, adv. Well, happy.
 III. n.
 1. Prosperity, Pañc. iii. d. 191; hail. Hit. 83, 10, M.M.
 2. Happiness, Böhtl. Ind. Spr. 1212.
 3. (with the dat. of the second person), A polite address, especially accompanying an advice, an objection, or expression of a different opinion; if you please, Rām. 3, 53, 2; Chr. 12, 3; 10, 5; with all respect for you, Chr. 11, 13; I beg your pardon, Rām. 3, 52, 37.
 4. Gold.
 5. Iron or steel.
 6. A fragrant grass, Cyperus, Ṛt. 1, 17 v. r.
 IV. m.
 1. Śiva.
 2. A wagtail.
 3. A bull.
 4. A heap.
 5. A fortune-teller, an impostor, Man. 9, 258.
 V. f. रा.
 1. The Ganges of heaven.
 2. A name of the second, seventh, and twelfth days of the lunar fortnight.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Goth. bats, bat + izo, bat + ista; A.S. bet; O.H.G. baz; Goth. ga-bat + non, bot + a, bot + jan; A.S. bót; Lat. fastus (for fad-tus), fastigium, fastidium, festivus (but festus belongs rather to भाष्).
भाद्र भाद्र, i. e. भद्र + अ, m. The name of a month, August--September.

भद्रक भद्र + क, adj., f. रिका.
 1. Beautiful, agreeable.
 2. Respectable, worthy, Daśak. in Chr. 195, 1.
 3. Good, Man. 9, 226.
भद्रंकर भद्रंकर, i. e. भद्र + म्-कर, adj., f. री, Propitious.
भाद्रमातुर भाद्रमातुर, i. e. भद्र-मातृ + अ, m. The son of a virtuous wife.
भद्र- + मुस्तक भद्र- + मुस्तक, n. = मुस्त, q. cf.
